top_categories.workout_context: At mile 60 of 126, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.

Road-specific control matters at Chasing Cancellara Zürich to Andermatt. Practice on point-to-point Alpine road ultra: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 126 miles.
113ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Chasing Cancellara Zürich to Andermatt's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before race day.
At Chasing Cancellara Zürich to Andermatt, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 126 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
14,222ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
14,222ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Chasing Cancellara Zürich to Andermatt. Train it until it feels boring.
126 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.

Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Chasing Cancellara Zürich to Andermatt. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Low-cadence force work supports 14,222ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.

race_overlay.heat: A pre-dawn start, exposed passes, and more than fifteen hours of possible weather create cold, rain, wind, and rapid temperature-change risk. Begin heat acclimatization 10–14 days before Chasing Cancellara Zürich to Andermatt — 20–30min sauna sessions or midday rides in full kit. Pre-load sodium 48 hours out. Target 500–750ml/hr with electrolytes on race day. Race-day realities: Hot valleys and cold passes.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Chasing Cancellara Zürich to Andermatt’s 126 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Altitude may change sustainable power and recovery at Chasing Cancellara Zürich to Andermatt. Use conservative pacing and test any travel strategy before the event.
race_overlay.terrain: The technical descents at Chasing Cancellara Zürich to Andermatt demand practice on similar paved roads. Ride point-to-point alpine road ultra at race-day cadence weekly. Practice braking points, corner entry, line choice, and accelerating smoothly out of turns. Confirm tire pressure and equipment before race week.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, Road Specific, and TT Threshold to prepare you for 126 miles of point-to-point alpine road ultra in Zürich to Andermatt, Switzerland.
